clue.text: Two honours — king and knave of hearts, for example

definitions.text: king and knave of hearts, for example

parts.note: in bridge the honours are the ace, king, queen, knave and ten, so two of them give ten and ace
in bridge the honours are the ace, king, queen, knave and ten, so two of them give ten and ace

explanation.surface: A card player describing two top cards, the king and jack of hearts.
explanation.walkthrough: Every across clue in this puzzle begins 'Two', each answer being two words run together. In bridge a tenace is a holding of two high cards with a gap between them, like king and knave.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridge holding of two high cards separated by one missing card, such as king and jack together, is that kind of combination.

clue.text: Stops working and leaves in vehicle

definitions.meaning: switches a machine off so that it no longer runs
a driver leaving a main road takes a side road

explanation.surface: A driver whose car stalls just as they exit the road.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to switch something off and to exit a road onto another while driving.

clue.text: When Einstein was adolescent — and wayward?

definitions.text: When Einstein was adolescent — and wayward?

indicators.note: wayward, meaning wandering off course, tells us the name's letters stray into a new order

explanation.surface: A remark about the young Einstein being a rebellious teenager.
explanation.walkthrough: Einstein was born in 1879, so he was a teenager in the 1890s; the whole clue is both the definition and, with 'wayward' rearranging his name, the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Born in 1879, the physicist was in his teens during the 1890s decade.

clue.text: Strike ruffian with clubs

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
a lout is a rough, uncouth man

explanation.surface: A thug hitting someone with clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: To clout is to hit hard, so it is a synonym for strike.

clue.text: Two problems with electricity providing quicker way

parts.note: a short (short circuit) and a cut (power cut) are both electrical faults
a short (short circuit) and a cut (power cut) are both electrical faults

explanation.surface: An electrician's troubles somehow leading to a faster route.
explanation.definitionFit: A route that saves time compared with the usual road is a quicker way.

clue.text: Cast on, with richly varied angelic voices

parts.note: to heave is to throw or cast

indicators.note: varied, meaning changed, signals that the letters of on and richly are rearranged

explanation.surface: A knitter casting on stitches with richly varied colours, plus a heavenly chorus.
explanation.definitionFit: A choir of angels singing in heaven is the classic picture of angelic voices.

clue.text: Again lay down sort of wine I got in English station

parts.note: red is a type of wine

indicators.note: got in means entered, so the letter I goes inside the word for station

parts.note: a post is a station or position someone is assigned to

explanation.surface: A wine merchant laying down bottles again at a station in England.
explanation.definitionFit: To deposit is to lay down, so the re- prefix makes it lay down once more.

clue.text: Caught wild bird or chicken

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a raven is a wild bird

explanation.surface: Someone catching either a wild bird or a domestic hen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chicken' looks like another bird beside the raven, but it means cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal or literary ways of calling someone cowardly.

clue.text: Stein's companion talks wildly about nothing

indicators.note: about means round, so the shuffled letters go around the zero
wildly signals that the letters of talks are thrown into disorder

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Gertrude Stein's friend chattering on excitedly about trivia.
explanation.walkthrough: TALKS rearranged gives TKLAS, and 'about' puts it around O.
explanation.definitionFit: Alice B. Toklas was the lifelong partner of the writer Gertrude Stein.

clue.text: Two circular things for a drummer

parts.note: a ring is circular, and the letter O is round too
a ring is circular, and the letter O is round too

explanation.surface: Two hoops or round objects being handed to a percussionist.
explanation.walkthrough: Ringo Starr was the drummer in the Beatles.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringo Starr is a famous example of a drummer, the one in the Beatles.

clue.text: Two supports withdraw from action

parts.note: a stand holds something up, and to back is to support
a stand holds something up, and to back is to support

explanation.surface: A pair of props being taken out of operation.
explanation.definitionFit: To step away and stay out of the fray is to withdraw from action; idiomatic phrase.

clue.text: Fear a ship sank disastrously, like a cutter

indicators.note: disastrously suggests things falling apart, so the words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: Worry that a vessel went down in catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutter' suggests a boat, matching the ship in the surface, but here it is a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutting tool is keen-edged, and this simile describes something very keen-edged.

clue.text: Two sorts of East European made to feel at home

indicators.note: sorts of, read as rearrangements, says the letters of the next word are shuffled
Two asks for the word East to be taken twice over before shuffling

explanation.surface: Two kinds of Eastern European person being welcomed warmly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two sorts of East' gives two different rearrangements of EAST side by side, SETA and TEAS; then E for European.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone at ease is to make them relaxed and comfortable, as if at home.

clue.text: Two Greek characters producing religious work

parts.note: pi and eta are two letters of the Greek alphabet
pi and eta are two letters of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Two letters from Greek combining to create a sacred work of art.
explanation.definitionFit: A pieta is a painting or sculpture of Mary holding the dead Christ, a classic devotional artwork.

clue.text: Two languages used in glossy cover

parts.note: French and Polish are both languages
French and Polish are both languages

explanation.surface: A bilingual coating with a shiny finish.
explanation.definitionFit: This shellac finish gives furniture a high-gloss protective coat, so it is a glossy cover.

clue.text: Military leader that exploits farm buildings

parts.note: CO is short for commanding officer
who can stand for that, as a relative pronoun
to exploit something is to use it

explanation.surface: An army commander who takes advantage of barns.
explanation.definitionFit: These are byres where cattle are kept, which are typical farm buildings.

clue.text: Destroyer's ruse at sea to protect stricken boat

indicators.note: to protect means to surround, so the mixed ruse wraps around the mixed boat
at sea, meaning confused, says the letters of ruse are mixed up
stricken, meaning damaged, tells us the letters of boat are jumbled

explanation.surface: A warship's trick on the ocean to shield a damaged vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Destroyer's' is read as 'destroyer is', and 'Destroyer' tempts towards a warship, matching the sea in the surface; it is a person who wrecks things.
explanation.definitionFit: One who deliberately wrecks or sabotages things is a destroyer.

clue.text: Curious new computer facility set up for poet

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means written upwards, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: nosy means curious
the net, the internet, is a computer facility

explanation.surface: An odd new piece of computer equipment installed for a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: NOSY + N + NET gives NOSYNNET, which 'set up' turns upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred, Lord Tennyson was a Victorian Poet Laureate.

clue.text: Two kinds of cheese found in London

parts.note: Swiss cheese and cottage cheese are both cheeses
Swiss cheese and cottage cheese are both cheeses

explanation.surface: A cheese lover discovering two varieties in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Swiss Cottage is a district of north-west London with a tube station.
explanation.definitionFit: This north London district is a place located in the capital, so the definition is a loose description.

clue.text: Basket-maker's tempestuous affair

indicators.note: tempestuous, meaning stormy, signals the letters of affair are churned up

explanation.surface: A stormy love affair involving a basket weaver.
explanation.definitionFit: Raffia is palm fibre used for weaving baskets, so it belongs to the basket weaver's craft.

clue.text: Violent desert wind in middle of Sahara leading to blunder

indicators.note: middle of takes the central letters of the word Sahara

parts.note: a boob is a silly mistake

explanation.surface: A sandstorm in the heart of the Sahara causing a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a fierce sandstorm of Sudan and the Sahara, a kind of violent desert wind.

clue.text: Two Tennessee neighbours in historic US mission

parts.note: Alabama (Ala) and Missouri (Mo) are states bordering Tennessee
Alabama (Ala) and Missouri (Mo) are states bordering Tennessee

explanation.surface: Two people living next door in Tennessee visiting an old American mission.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alamo in San Antonio was a Spanish mission, famous for the 1836 siege.

clue.text: Two places in Ireland very cheap

parts.note: Knock is a village in County Mayo with a shrine, and Down is a county in Northern Ireland
Knock is a village in County Mayo with a shrine, and Down is a county in Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A traveller finding two Irish towns where everything costs little.
explanation.definitionFit: A knock-down price is one heavily reduced, so the phrase is an idiom for very cheap.

clue.text: Part of book, apparently, that's between parts of 12

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A section of a book seemingly sitting between parts of something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 is PIETA, made of PI and ETA; in the Greek alphabet kappa comes after eta and before pi.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek alphabetical order the tenth letter lies between eta and pi, the two letters of the earlier answer.

clue.text: Two friers going wrong, smelling worse

indicators.note: going wrong suggests the letters before it are put out of order

explanation.surface: A pair of chip-shop fryers malfunctioning and giving off an ever stronger stink.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 'Two' is not a theme word but fodder: TWO plus FRIERS rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Frowsty means stale and musty, so the comparative form describes something more stuffy and smelly.

clue.text: Two European rivers put in verse

parts.note: the Po flows through Italy and the Ems through Germany
the Po flows through Italy and the Ems through Germany

explanation.surface: Two continental rivers being written into poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Poems are compositions in verse, so the plural noun and mass noun match in sense.

clue.text: Two presidents behind American attacks

indicators.note: behind places the two presidents after the American

parts.note: George H. W. Bush and George W. Bush were both US presidents, hence two Bushes

explanation.surface: Two leaders following an American in launching assaults.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambushes are surprise attacks from hiding, so the verb or plural noun fits attacks.

clue.text: Two men named benefactor

parts.note: Pat and Ron are both men's names
Pat and Ron are both men's names

explanation.surface: Two named men singled out as generous sponsors.
explanation.definitionFit: A patron gives financial support to an artist or cause, making them a benefactor.
